result.target_summary: Intel relies on third-party IP and technology licenses, which may not be available on commercially reasonable terms or at all. Failure to obtain necessary licenses could preclude sales of certain products or materially impact financial results. Additionally, open-source software usage may require public disclosure of source code.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation: The 2024 disclosure D141 focuses specifically on risks related to third-party IP licensing, open-source software compliance, and legal/regulatory requirements. The 2023 disclosures in the proposed group (D122, D131, D132, D133, D152) relate to supply chain logistics, manufacturing capacity, and geopolitical risks, which are distinct topics. No 2023 disclosure covers IP licensing or open-source software risks, so no counterpart exists for D141.

peer_results.rationale: The retrieved candidates (amd_2024_7_D047 and amd_2024_7_D041) concern unconditional purchase commitments for wafers/IP licenses and the immaterial impact of Pillar Two tax legislation, respectively. Neither addresses the specific risk of failing to obtain essential third-party IP or technology licenses required for product design and sales, nor the open-source compliance risks cited by Intel.

The retrieved candidates (avgo_2024_7_D068 and avgo_2024_7_D030) discuss risks related to acquisition financing availability and compliance conditions for tax incentives. These are distinct from Intel's disclosure regarding the availability of third-party intellectual property licenses and open-source software obligations.

The retrieved candidates (mu_2024_7_D026 and mu_2024_7_D025) focus on the impact of global tax reforms and OECD Pillar Two legislation on tax expenses. These tax-related risks are not comparable to Intel's operational risk concerning third-party IP dependency and open-source licensing.

comparisons.peer_summary: Nvidia may seek licenses for customers requiring restricted products but has no assurance that the USG will grant them, act timely, or act at all.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Nvidia disclose risks regarding the uncertainty of obtaining necessary third-party licenses or government approvals to sell their products, highlighting a dependency on external permissions that may not be granted. Intel warns that failure to obtain third-party IP licenses could preclude product sales, while Nvidia notes it has no assurance that the USG will grant required export licenses for certain customers.

sentences.text: Failure to obtain the right to use third-party technology, or to license IP on commercially reasonable terms, could preclude us from selling certain products or otherwise have a material adverse impact on our financial condition and operating results.

To the extent that a customer requires products covered by the licensing requirements, we may seek a license for the customer but have no assurance that the USG will grant such a license, or that the USG will act on the license application in a timely manner or at all.
